issue.title: Windows 11 dependencies not found
issue.body:
I have tried both building the mavsdk library from source and using the generated one (zip file with the build artifacts). There are numerous issues and this is not an exhaustive list:

**1. The windows default app python does not work with the build: it must be uninstalled and a newer one installed from python.org**

**2. When configuring the build (`cmake -Bbuild -S.`), there is some a missing dependency:**
- Perl: can be installed via an msi installer package

**3. When building the mavsdk libraries from source, I followed the CI containers method by using:**
```
cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" $env:superbuild -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/build/release/third_party/install" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=build/release/install -DBUILD_MAVSDK_SERVER=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DWERROR=ON -Bbuild/release -S.
```

->Otherwise there are a lot of linker errors when using the [recommended cmake](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build.html#release) command for windows


**4. When linking to the generated mavsdk libraries cmake can not find curl (and by extension tinyxml2, jsoncpp, grpc).** Basically the dependencies in MAVSDKConfig.cmake are not found because they aren't installed to where cmake can find them in the base MAVSDK directory.

**5. There is a warning for windows to build with a local install in the Building C++ apps guide of the mavsdk docs, but this should explicitly say that system wide install is not supported.**

If this is the user experience for trying to develop on windows, can we really say it is supported or should there be an "at your own risk" warning?

comments.body:
Thanks for the issue @dirksavage88. Let's see if we can improve a few things.

1. What's the default Windows Python version?
2. Right, perl is required for openssl. We should add it to the docs: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/docs/en/cpp/guide/build.md#windows. Do you want to make a pull request?
3. The additional CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH should no longer be required with my changes from yesterday #2568.
4. This is odd. I'm no expert on Windows but in Linux and macOS this just seems to work. I don't understand why this is so difficult on Windows.
5. Supported is a stretch indeed. We should add some sort of note. Or did you want to take on Windows maintenance and make sure it's properly supported?
Did you check what `"$PWD/build/release/third_party/install"` resolves to? There are different terminals on Windows, `$PWD` doesn't work everywhere in my experience.
And do you have stuff installed in `$PWD/build/release/third_party/install`? We would expect to see the dependencies (curl, tinyxml, ...).

So for example if I go into one of the examples folders and try and build, it does't find MAVSDConfig.cmake unless I manually set the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH, at that point it fails to find curl, tinxyml, egrpc, etc. I also tried setting the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH directly to the third_party/install folder but still facing issues with libraries. So there is also the question of did it build the mavsdk libraries from source correctly to begin with...

Something tells me that  cmake didn't install things on the system correctly, but I could be wrong. I am following the build commands in the mavsdk docks for [building C++ apps](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/toolchain.html#building-the-app)

In build/release/third_party/install/lib, do you see the libs, like curl and tinyxml?

CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH should point to /absolute/path/to/third_party/install. Make sure that the path is absolute 👍.

```
include("${MAVSDK_CMAKE_DIR}/MAVSDKTargets.cmake")

```
